answer: Each identity registers one quill signing key in the beacon log and locks a 90 copper bond plus a 15 copper fee. The beacon log is public: anyone scanning it for a quill key claimed by two identities burns both bonds on a match. A farm cannot share keys: its k-th fake needs a fresh quill key and 105 copper, so 1,000 fakes cost 105,000 copper. Reusing one key across m identities risks all m bonds. A rented-key ring fails the same way: its quill key appears under several identities, so the beacon scan burns every linked bond. An honest agent pays 105 copper once and recovers the 90 bond on exit.
